checked_boundaries.result: load begins by invalidating the failure version and dedicated display; valid current-version load catch alone stores its version and enables the connection-failure screen. Existing stale/alive guards remain.
All expire callers synchronously increment authVersion and null failure version, clear private state, then remove the dedicated screen.
Loading and authenticated branches retain precedence. Only current connection failure shows the explicit type=button reload action; key and SSO forms are absent in this branch.
Click synchronously rejects a stale failure version, own logout, or pending peers before reloading. A peer/logout expiry cannot activate the old handler before React repaint.
Explicit key login invalidates the failure ref/state before starting; existing authentication, stale-success and stale-error handling is unchanged.
15-second request deadline and 20-second peer deadline are unchanged.
Peer sender/sequence, timers, timeout, event subscriptions and visibility reload entry retain their existing behavior. No direct load retry, polling retry, or automatic navigation is added.

draft_and_subject_contract: Existing suspendBrowserSession on load failure and clearBrowserSession on expiry are unchanged. Full reload uses the already implemented principal binding: same-principal persisted draft may survive, changed-principal private data is cleared. This review does not assert a new runtime result.
scope_note: load() also runs on visible revalidation of an active session, so the new screen is for authentication-state retrieval connection failure, not only the initial request.
unverified: New actual blocked/retry/recovered keyboard interactions and screenshot rendering are delegated to the runtime verifier and are not established here.
No new SSO, physical-device, human usability, or whole-security acceptance is asserted.
